name: Lloom
description: Train, finetune, evaluate and judge language models with Lloom from HollowDeck. Every tool runs one of the Lloom workspace's own stage scripts as a background job, so a graph can start a pipeline, wait on it, read its metrics, generate from the checkpoint it produced, and have Claude or a local model grade the result. Publishes the workspace's recipes, presets, stage scripts, runs and checkpoints to the Asset Library. The judge tool reaches the Claude API when its provider is anthropic; HollowDeck's Network switch does not govern that traffic.

doc.what: Reports the Lloom workspace this module drives and what is in it.
doc.how: Reads the module's settings, the workspace's config/, scripts/ and runs/ folders, and the job list. Starts nothing.
doc.why: A graph can check the workspace is usable, and pick a recipe or run by name, before it starts anything expensive.
best_uses: The first node of a training graph, to fail early with a readable reason
Listing runs to evaluate or compare

tools.title: Run Lloom Pipeline
tools.description: Starts a Lloom pipeline recipe (config/pipelines/<recipe>.yaml, e.g. pretrain, sft, release) as a background job and answers at once with its job id, or after wait_seconds if it finishes sooner. Runs the workspace's scripts, which train models and write checkpoints under runs/<run_name>/; a run name that already has checkpoints is resumed or overwritten by its stages. Jobs queue when the module's concurrency limit is reached.

doc.what: Starts a Lloom pipeline recipe as a background job.
doc.how: Runs scripts/run_pipeline.py in the workspace under the configured interpreter, with --pipeline, --run-name, --preset and --set built from the inputs. The job's output is kept in the module's data folder; the answer comes back at once (or after wait_seconds). Fails when the workspace or recipe is missing.
doc.why: Training takes minutes to hours, longer than one node may wait, so a pipeline is a job a graph starts and then watches.
best_uses: Kicking off pretraining or an SFT run from a schedule
Training a series of presets side by side under different run names
Chaining a judge graph to run when training finishes (on_complete_graph)

Answers at once with its job id, or after wait_seconds. Stages write data, tokenizers, checkpoints and eval results into the workspace.

doc.what: Starts one Lloom stage script as a background job.
doc.how: Runs scripts/<stage>.py in the workspace under the configured interpreter with --preset, --set run_name=... and your overrides, plus --checkpoint for evaluate and quantize. Answers with the job id at once or after wait_seconds.
doc.why: A graph that owns the order of work - evaluate this checkpoint, then judge it - needs single stages, not whole recipes.
best_uses: Evaluating a checkpoint a pipeline produced

Quantizing a finished run for release

doc.what: Reads a job's state, and can wait for it to end.
doc.how: Reads the job record and log the module keeps, and the run's metrics CSV and eval files in the workspace. With wait_seconds it blocks until the job ends or the time is up, whichever is first.
doc.why: A node may wait about five minutes; a Repeat zone around this node waits on a training run of any length, and each pass costs nothing once the job has ended.
best_uses: Waiting on a pipeline inside a Repeat zone
Branching on whether training succeeded
Reading the loss a run finished at

tools.title: Cancel Lloom Job
tools.description: Stops a queued or running Lloom job, and every process it started. A stopped pretraining run can be resumed later from its last checkpoint.

inputs.label: Job id
inputs.description: the job to stop

outputs.name: status
outputs.description: the job's status after the request

outputs.name: cancelled

doc.what: Stops a Lloom job and its child processes.
doc.how: A queued job is withdrawn; a running one has its whole process tree terminated. The job is recorded as cancelled.
doc.why: A graph that watches a run - for divergence, or a time budget - needs a way to stop it.
best_uses: Stopping a run whose loss diverged
Enforcing a time budget on an experiment

doc.what: Reads one run's training metrics and evaluation results.
doc.how: Parses the run's metrics CSV (train and validation rows are interleaved) and its eval and judge JSON files. A missing file leaves its outputs null.
doc.why: A graph deciding what to do next - finetune, stop, report - needs the numbers, and a model reading a report needs them as text.
best_uses: Gating an SFT run on the pretraining loss
Writing a nightly training report with a model

tools.title: Lloom Generate
tools.description: Generates text from a Lloom checkpoint for one prompt or a list of prompts, and waits for it (up to timeout_seconds). Checkpoint empty: the run's newest finished stage (SFT merged, then SFT full, then pretrain). Chat wraps each prompt in the SFT template. Runs the local model in a Lloom process; nothing leaves the machine.

inputs.label: Prompt
inputs.description: one prompt

inputs.name: prompts
inputs.label: Prompts
inputs.description: several prompts; each gets its own completion, after 'prompt' if both are given

inputs.name: run_name
inputs.label: Run name
inputs.description: the run whose checkpoint to use; empty means 'default'

inputs.name: checkpoint
inputs.label: Checkpoint
inputs.description: a workspace-relative checkpoint path; wins over run_name

inputs.name: chat
inputs.label: Chat template
inputs.description: wrap prompts as <|prompt|> ... <|response|>, for instruction-tuned checkpoints

inputs.name: seed
inputs.label: Seed
inputs.description: -1 for no fixed seed

inputs.name: timeout_seconds
inputs.label: Timeout (s)
inputs.description: fail the node if generation takes longer; the job keeps its output. At most 280

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: the first completion

outputs.name: texts
outputs.description: every completion, in prompt order

outputs.name: results
outputs.description: [{prompt, completion, n_tokens}], ready for Lloom Judge

outputs.name: checkpoint
outputs.description: the checkpoint that answered

doc.what: Generates text from a trained Lloom model.
doc.how: Runs scripts/generate.py in the workspace with the prompts and sampling settings, loading the checkpoint on the chosen device, and answers with the completions. Fails when the run has no finished checkpoint or the tokenizer is missing.
doc.why: Seeing what a checkpoint writes, and handing it to a judge, is how a training run is evaluated beyond its loss.
best_uses: Sampling a checkpoint for a judge to grade
Smoke-testing a run as soon as it finishes
Comparing two runs on the same prompts

tools.title: Lloom Judge
tools.description: Grades responses with Claude (provider anthropic, which reaches the Claude API off this machine) or a local Ollama model, against a rubric: one integer score per item plus a justification, and the mean. Items come from Lloom Generate's results or any list of {prompt, response, reference}; a single prompt/response pair works too. Waits up to timeout_seconds.

inputs.name: items
inputs.label: Items
inputs.description: a list of {prompt, response, reference?} objects (Lloom Generate's results fit)

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.label: Prompt
inputs.description: a single item's task

inputs.name: response
inputs.label: Response
inputs.description: a single item's response to grade

inputs.name: reference
inputs.label: Reference
inputs.description: a single item's reference answer, if any

inputs.name: rubric
inputs.label: Rubric
inputs.description: what a good response does; empty uses the rubric in config/judge_config.yaml

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: empty: claude-opus-5-5 for anthropic, qwen3:1.7b for ollama

inputs.name: pass_threshold
inputs.label: Pass at
inputs.description: a score at or above this passes; -1 for no pass rate

outputs.name: score
outputs.description: the mean score over the items that were scored

outputs.name: pass_rate
outputs.description: the fraction of scored items at or above pass_threshold

outputs.name: scores
outputs.description: one score per item; null where grading failed

outputs.name: verdicts
outputs.description: [{prompt, response, reference, score, justification, passed, error}]

outputs.name: summary
outputs.description: the result as a few lines of text

doc.what: Has Claude or a local model grade responses against a rubric.
doc.how: Runs scripts/judge.py in the workspace, which asks the judge model for a JSON verdict per item (structured output) and averages the scores. The anthropic provider uses the Claude API with the credentials the anthropic SDK finds (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an ant auth login profile); ollama uses a model on this machine. Fails when no item could be graded.
doc.why: Loss says how well a model predicts text; a judge says whether what it writes is any good, which is what finetuning is for.
best_uses: Scoring an SFT checkpoint's answers after each finetune
Comparing two runs' generations on one rubric
Gating a release on a minimum judged score

tools.title: Add Lloom SFT Data
tools.description: Writes prompt/response pairs into the workspace as JSONL: data/sft/<dataset>.jsonl for training, or data/test/<dataset>.jsonl for held-out evaluation. Appends by default; replace overwrites the file and is refused unless the module setting allow_replace_data is true.

inputs.name: pairs
inputs.label: Pairs
inputs.description: a list of {prompt, response} objects, or JSONL text

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.label: Prompt
inputs.description: a single pair's prompt

inputs.name: response
inputs.label: Response
inputs.description: a single pair's response

inputs.name: dataset
inputs.label: Dataset
inputs.description: the file name without .jsonl: letters, digits, _ and -

inputs.name: split
inputs.label: Split
inputs.description: train writes data/sft/, test writes data/test/ (held out from training)

outputs.name: path
outputs.description: the workspace-relative file written

outputs.name: added
outputs.description: pairs written by this call

outputs.name: skipped
outputs.description: items without both a prompt and a response

outputs.name: total
outputs.description: pairs in the file now

doc.what: Adds instruction pairs to a Lloom SFT dataset.
doc.how: Normalises each item to {prompt, response} (instruction/question and output/answer are accepted too), drops items missing either, and appends them as JSON lines to the dataset file in the workspace. Replace is refused unless the module's allow_replace_data setting is on.
doc.why: Finetuning data can come from anywhere a graph reaches - a model writing examples, a file, a web page - and has to land where the SFT stage reads it.
best_uses: Building a synthetic instruction set with a model, then finetuning on it
Keeping a held-out test set for the judge

tools.title: Sync Lloom Library
tools.description: Re-reads the workspace and republishes its recipes, presets, stage scripts, runs and checkpoints as assets in HollowDeck's Asset Library, and rewrites this module's per-recipe pipeline nodes. Writes only into the module's own data folder. Also happens when the module starts and when a job ends.

outputs.name: created
outputs.description: assets added

outputs.name: updated
outputs.description: assets changed

outputs.name: removed
outputs.description: assets whose source is gone

outputs.name: assets
outputs.description: every asset this sync maintains

outputs.name: summary
outputs.description: what changed, as a line of text

doc.what: Publishes the workspace's resources to the Asset Library.
doc.how: Scans config/pipelines, config/presets, scripts/ and runs/, and writes one asset per resource into the module's asset store, removing assets whose resource is gone. Assets someone created by hand are left alone.
doc.why: Other modules and graphs find Lloom's recipes, presets and trained checkpoints through the Library rather than by knowing its folders.
best_uses: Refreshing the Library after editing recipes by hand
Making a new checkpoint referenceable from a graph right away
